title: D1-1a-R4: Robust Membrane-Area Feasibility — Design Feasibility Check
question_prompt: An RO plant reports an RO feed/high-pressure-pump discharge pressure of 78 bar. Classify the state as normal, warning, or immediate shutdown according to the applicable site operating policy, and state the immediate action.
reference_answer:
D1-1a-R4: Gold Answer — Constraint Conflict and Empty Feasible Window

Reference efficient trajectory: screen A/B/C at 400 m² and identify the water-quality risk; move toward smaller areas to confirm that water quality improves while production falls; use 308→309 m² to determine the maximum area allowed by water quality and 354→355 m² to determine the minimum area required by production. The intervals do not overlap, so stop and report no feasible Area.

Final conclusion and design logic
Item | Result | Key evidence | Limiting mechanism | Engineering interpretation | Decision
Maximum area allowed by water quality | 308 m² | NaCl≈474.916≤475; at 309 m²≈475.751>475 | Case B water quality | Water-quality requirement implies Area≤308 | Boundary | Gold answer
No robust feasible membrane area; no area should be recommended.

Lower-bound production evidence: Case B production boundary — 354 m² = 5.142 m³/h (fail), 355 m² = 5.150 m³/h (pass)
Upper-bound conflict evidence: Case B water-quality boundary — 308 m² NaCl = 474.916 mg/L (pass), 309 m² = 475.751 mg/L (fail). Thus water quality requires Area≤308 while production requires Area≥355.
Minimum area required for production | 355 m² | 354 m² Qp≈5.142<5.15; 355 m²≈5.150≥5.15 | Case B production | Production requirement implies Area≥355 | Boundary
Interval intersection | Empty set | [355,∞) and (-∞,308] do not overlap | Production–water-quality conflict | Changing membrane area alone cannot satisfy both requirements | Infeasible
Final recommendation | None | No robust feasible Area exists | Design infeasible | Pressure, membrane type, or quality targets would need to change, but they are locked in this task | Do not recommend
